title: On Monday's show: Public Defender Charlie Cofer; 'Florida Before Flagler' - NewsBreak
text: 1 days ago For years, the state Department of Children and Families has allowed patients with diagnosed mental illness to remain in city and county jails rather than admit them to state psychiatric facilities. The practice is against state law: Florida Statutes require mentally incompetent defendants to be placed in state custody within 15 days. The state has failed to meet the standard for hundreds of patients. DCF’s own data show the average wait is 124 days. State officials attribute the lapse to a shortage of forensic hospital beds. And according to a new lawsuit, the state isn’t moving to correct the problem. Though Florida needs an estimated 2,034 new beds if it wants to meet industry standards by 2029, and 1,602 new beds just to maintain its current occupancy rate, DCF didn't seek any money for new beds in the 2026-’27 budget. We talk to one of the plaintiffs in the case about why they’ve chosen to bring their concerns to federal court. Read full article
